methodology.timing: Process wall in measurements; library wall excluding TPC-H pool initialization in library_measurements. Library timing includes table/session/job creation, worker startup/join, generation and batch consumption.
methodology.cpu_and_rss: Whole fresh process, including setup. Ordered Populate consumers run on the calling thread; reference partitions consume/drop on their workers. Reference comparisons therefore include delivery-semantics differences; before/after comparisons keep the ordered API.
methodology.output: Full Arrow RecordBatches are generated and consumed; no IPC encoding, file output, disk flushing or cache drops.
methodology.scale: SF10 only. SF100 was not run.
methodology.reference: This integration campaign compares Populate on new main against the merged optimized implementation. Rust library comparisons remain in the earlier reports and retain their recorded revisions.
methodology.aggregate: Shared per-source ordered delivery; compatible sales/returns stay fused. SSB-flat is measured separately and its dimension preparation is timed.
methodology.controls: stream consumes/drops each batch on its worker; TPC-DS stream is unfused. Do not attribute an ordered-fused versus stream-unfused difference solely to buffering.

learning_list.method: Fresh processes, matched mimalloc allocator and release flags, one warmup followed by seven alternating baseline/candidate runs. Library wall time excludes TPC-H text-pool initialization; process CPU and RSS include it. Generation produces full Arrow batches without disk output. Correctness checks are timed separately.

learnings.finding: Default chunks leave small tables underparallelized.
learnings.evidence: Earlier SF10 controls: supplier 11.87 to 2.62 ms, customer 27.48 to 9.47 ms with 8192-row chunks; those are exploratory measurements from revision 90ef414.
learnings.status: implement and remeasure against current main

learnings.finding: Ordered chunk delivery retains substantial Arrow memory.
learnings.evidence: Earlier matched mimalloc controls: lineitem 2.61 GiB ordered versus 0.59 GiB worker-consumed; TPC-DS store_sales 6.58 versus 0.21 GiB. The worker-consumed experiment changes callback semantics and is not a drop-in replacement.
learnings.status: reduce buffering while preserving ordered callback semantics

learnings.finding: Allocator choice materially changes parallel generation results.
learnings.evidence: The CLIs use mimalloc, while the library inherits the application allocator. Both sides must use the same allocator.

learnings.finding: Full ordered value checks reveal buffering costs with a slow consumer.
learnings.evidence: Updated-main TPC-H SF10 serialization/hash peak RSS was 6.10 GiB versus 1.94 GiB for the adaptive-chunk candidate. This is a validation workload, not the generation benchmark.

learnings.finding: A bounded completion channel does not bound the pending reorder map.
learnings.evidence: populate-table/src/sched.rs drains completions into per-source BTreeMaps while waiting for each next chunk. Subdividing chunks reduces bytes per result but does not enforce a global outstanding-result memory cap.
learnings.status: source observation; scheduler memory-cap behavior unchanged

experiments.name: TPC-H shared scheduler
experiments.finding: Largest-first SF10 median 283.52 to 269.81 ms (seven runs); canonical table order unchanged within noise; peak RSS reduced in both orders; single-thread unchanged within noise.

experiments.name: TPC-H adaptive Arrow chunks
experiments.finding: Supplier 4.69x, customer 2.70x, part 2.21x, lineitem 1.10x versus scheduler-only. Small-table RSS increases with active workers; lineitem RSS falls from 2.55 to 1.40 GiB. All-table generation improves about 3.5% beyond scheduler change. Parquet/text writer paths unchanged.
experiments.validation: All eight full SF10 ordered table serializations have equal SHA-256 hashes; crate tests pass, including reference Arrow/text equality, deep SF10/SF1000 ranges, arbitrary chunking, Parquet roundtrips and repeated/empty multi-table inputs.

experiments.name: Main advanced during optimization
experiments.finding: Main independently adopted the shared TPC-H scheduler and DynTable. Final comparisons use 90c9d39b; the final PR delta is adaptive chunk sizing, including a reusable DynTable.parallel_chunks method. Earlier scheduler measurements remain historical evidence.

experiments.name: TPC-DS adaptive Arrow chunks
experiments.status: accepted; all 24 full SF10 table hashes match updated main
experiments.finding: Against updated main, all-table SF10 median 528.42 to 386.81 ms and median process peak RSS 8.42 to 2.67 GiB across seven runs. Item 15.47x, customer 9.11x, customer_address 10.14x. Sales/returns pairing retained. Catalog paired timings overlap; no paired catalog speedup claim.

experiments.name: Tiny TPC-DS dimensions
experiments.finding: The guard restores household_demographics from 0.429 to 0.346 ms and 20.9 to 12.9 MiB peak RSS; all-table timings overlap (390.88 versus 388.04 ms).

experiments.name: Final accepted implementation
experiments.finding: Matched mimalloc: TPC-H main 268.25 to 258.53 ms, TPC-DS main 532.01 to 386.49 ms. Matched system allocator: TPC-H 417.30 to 306.93 ms, TPC-DS 857.21 to 703.84 ms. System allocator baselines are noisier; inspect all seven samples and ranges. Rust reference aggregate medians are 502.46 ms (TPC-H) and 829.87 ms (TPC-DS), with optimized Populate 258.80 and 387.49 ms in those paired comparisons.

experiments.name: SSB adaptive Arrow chunks
experiments.status: accepted: all five full SF10 base tables and lineorder_flat have matching ordered text hashes; crate tests pass
experiments.finding: Seven-run SF10 medians: part 44.00 to 7.81 ms; customer 17.30 to 4.32 ms; all five tables 82.70 to 77.27 ms (ranges nearly touch). Aggregate RSS 1.99 to 1.18 GiB. lineorder_flat 379.44 to 353.81 ms and 4.11 to 1.91 GiB. Flat dimension preparation is inside the library timing.

experiments.name: DSB subdivide every table
experiments.finding: All-table median regressed 887.48 to 1031.04 ms despite lower RSS. Catalog returns 355.26 to 413.97 ms; store returns 466.48 to 583.62 ms. The DSB paired row generators are initialized per chunk and respond differently from TPC-DS direct column kernels.

experiments.name: DSB dimensions and inventory only
experiments.status: accepted: all 24 full SF10 ordered text hashes match baseline; crate tests pass
experiments.finding: All-table median 892.04 to 830.81 ms. Item 184.90 to 14.45 ms; customer_address 99.16 to 11.72 ms; channel timings restored within noise. Aggregate peak RSS rises 3.89 to 4.37 GiB as more dimension workers participate. Single-thread controls are unchanged within noise.

experiments.name: SSB/DSB system allocator controls
experiments.finding: SSB-flat improves from 766.02 to 553.70 ms. DSB aggregate 1403.61 to 1378.25 ms has broadly overlapping ranges (1193.92–1454.00 and 1258.46–1512.92 ms): no reliable system-allocator aggregate DSB speedup claim.

experiments.name: Ready-chunk scheduler fast path
experiments.status: rejected: no reliable aggregate improvement; patch reverted
experiments.finding: Seven alternating SF10 runs per implementation and case. TPC-H all 257.10 to 257.55 ms; TPC-DS all 383.82 to 385.23 ms; SSB all 75.29 to 76.80 ms; SSB-flat 350.14 to 350.33 ms; DSB all 834.90 to 832.34 ms. Ranges overlap in all seven cases, including TPC-H lineitem and TPC-DS inventory. Scheduler order/error tests passed.

experiments.name: Integration after main advanced to 78001b44
experiments.status: accepted after fresh SF10 benchmarks, full ordered hashes and workspace checks
experiments.finding: Main migrated SSB to DynTable and updated shared string helpers. Resolve the SSB import conflict and use the existing DynTable.parallel_chunks helper for SSB. The final optimization diff is 13 files, 244 insertions and 15 deletions relative to new main. Historical benchmark reports retain their exact earlier revisions.

validation.strict_clippy: Both unchanged main 78001b44 and candidate reproduce clippy::chunks_exact_to_as_chunks, first at populate-core/src/string.rs:168. The earlier main also reports this lint in lehmer.rs:146. Allowing only this lint passes the candidate workspace.
validation.dsb_reference_caveat: DSB native-C item mismatch remains. Optimization hashes compare Populate before/after; this does not establish equivalence to native DSB.

stopping_review.decision: Stop: no further demonstrated simple improvement after reviewing the hot paths and rejecting the scheduler fast path.
observations: TPC-H flat_map already reserves exact child counts and reads source rows in place. Further loop specialization would broaden the change.

TPC-H comment views already separate independent random pool reads, read only the required prefix for long comments, and request huge pages. Further memory-access tuning would need architecture-sensitive experiments.

TPC-DS sales already fuse sales/returns and generate columns directly with packed validity bits. The profile is dominated by channel generation and pricing; changing these would broaden the change and touch RNG/reference-sensitive logic.
Changing ordered caller-thread delivery or introducing persistent workers/global buffering control would alter the system design. Those paths were not adopted.
The previously tested DSB channel subdivision regressed throughput; retaining the accepted selective chunk sizing avoids that regression.
stopping_review.integration: A main-branch advancement was detected at the final PR check; integrate it and revalidate the accepted behavior without adding another optimization.

specification.sampling: One excluded warmup and seven alternating fresh-process runs for 32-thread timings; three for one-thread controls. Complete output hashes use one run per implementation without warmup.
specification.source_notes: New main is 78001b44; candidate is 1a89e1d1 with parents 4bd856d0 and 78001b44. Main changed SSB to DynTable; SSB now calls the existing parallel_chunks helper. Other accepted chunk adaptations remain unchanged. Prior comparisons are historical, with their own revisions.
specification.reproduction: Build the matching probe against each recorded commit with the saved lockfile and release profile, using --features mimalloc. Each exact command and executable SHA-256 is recorded.
